problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=4x\operatorname{ln}⁡y,\,y(2)=e
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method. What entry should be placed in the column for $Δy$ in the second row of the table below if the step size is $Δx=\frac{1}{2}?$

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $2$ | $e$ | $8$ | $4$ |
| $$ | $$ | $$ | $\,?\,$ |

feedback.problem:
Consider the following initial value problem:

$$
{y}^{′}=\frac{x{y}^{2}}{4},\,y(1)=2
$$

We wish to approximate the solution using Euler's method. What entry should be placed in the column for $Δy$ in the second row of the table below if the step size is $Δx=2?$ 

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| $$ | $$ | $$ | $\,?\,$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
To get the values of $x$ and $y$ in the second row, we add $Δx$ to $x$ and $Δy$ to $y,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3 \\ {y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =2+2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| $3$ | $4$ | $$ | $$ |

Next, we compute ${y}^{′}$ according to the given rule (using the values of $x$ and $y$ in the second row), and we compute 
$Δy$ using Euler's method:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{x{y}^{2}}{4} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot {4}^{2}}{4} \\  & =12 \\ Δy & ={y}^{′}\cdot Δx \\  & =12\cdot 2 \\  & =24\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $\,Δy\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| $3$ | $4$ | $12$ | $24$ |
